literal: Shenwu was about to go; Heba Yanguo'er asked to delay the march to exhaust them.
idiomatic: Gao Huan was preparing to march when Heba Yanguo'er urged him to go slowly and wear the enemy down.

literal: Shenwu then often dawdled, pleading that without a bridge over the river he could not cross.
idiomatic: Gao Huan deliberately lingered, claiming there was no bridge and he could not cross the river.

literal: Bu Fan's army was strong; Zhao was defeated and fled.
idiomatic: Bu Fan's forces grew overwhelming and Erzhu Zhao was beaten and fled.

literal: Initially, when Xiaozhuang executed Erzhu Rong, knowing his faction would surely harbor treasonous designs, he secretly ordered Bu Fan to strike their rear.
idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Xiaozhuang killed Erzhu Rong, he knew the Erzhu faction would rebel and secretly ordered Bu Fan to attack them from the rear.

literal: After Bu Fan had defeated Zhao and the others, as his military strength daily grew, Zhao again asked Shenwu for rescue.
idiomatic: Once Bu Fan had routed Erzhu Zhao, his army grew stronger by the day, and Zhao turned again to Gao Huan for help.

literal: Shenwu inwardly plotted against Zhao, yet also feared that if Bu Fan were left later he would be hard to eliminate; he therefore joined Zhao with full force to break him.
idiomatic: Gao Huan intended to destroy Zhao but feared Bu Fan would prove still harder to remove later, so he joined Zhao and broke Bu Fan between them.

literal: When Fan died, Zhao deeply felt gratitude toward Shenwu and swore brotherhood.
idiomatic: After Bu Fan fell, Erzhu Zhao was deeply grateful to Gao Huan and swore brotherhood with him.

literal: At that time Shilong, Dulü, and Yanbo jointly wielded court governance; Tianguang held the pass west, Zhao held Bing Province, Zhongyuan held Dong Commandery — each amassed troops and acted as tyrants, and the realm suffered bitterly.
idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong, Dulü, and Yanbo held the court; Tianguang held the west, Zhao held Bing Province, and Zhongyuan held Dong Commandery—each tyrannized with armed force, and all under heaven groaned.

literal: Ge Rong's followers who had flowed into Bing and Si numbered over two hundred thousand; oppressed by the Jie-Hu they could not live, and there were twenty-six uprisings large and small; half were executed, yet scattered pillaging still did not cease.
idiomatic: More than two hundred thousand of Ge Rong's followers had drifted into Bing and Si; bullied by the Jie-Hu, they could scarcely survive. There were twenty-six rebellions, large and small; half the rebels were killed, yet brigandage never stopped.

literal: Zhao was troubled by this and asked Shenwu for a plan.
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao was vexed by this and asked Gao Huan's counsel.

literal: Shenwu said: "The rebel remnants of the Six Garrisons cannot all be killed; you should choose men who are by nature close to Your Highness and privately appoint them to command them.
idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "The Six Garrisons rebels cannot all be slaughtered. Send men you trust in private to command them.

literal: If there are offenders, punish only their commanders, then those punished will be few.
idiomatic: When crimes occur, punish only the commander, and few will suffer.

literal: " Zhao said: "Good — who can undertake this?
idiomatic: Zhao said, "Well said—who should take it?"

literal: Heba Yun was then seated there and recommended Shenwu.
idiomatic: Heba Yun, who was present, named Gao Huan.

literal: Shenwu punched and beat him, breaking one tooth, and said: "In the lifetime when the Heavenly Pillar lived, you fellows submitted to orders like hawks and hounds. Today the realm rests under Your Highness's arrangement, yet Ajuni dares falsely accuse subordinates and deceive superiors — I ask that he be killed.
idiomatic: Gao Huan struck him with his fist and broke a tooth, saying, "In the days of the Heavenly Pillar you crawled to his commands like hunting dogs. The realm now rests with you, my lord, yet this flatterer dares deceive you—I ask leave to kill him.

literal: Zhao took Shenwu as sincere and thereupon entrusted it to him.
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao took Gao Huan for sincere and entrusted the command to him.

literal: Shenwu, because Zhao was drunk, feared that when sober he might grow suspicious and doubtful; he therefore went out and proclaimed that having received commission to command the garrison troops of the province, they could assemble east of the Fen to receive orders.
idiomatic: While Zhao was drunk, Gao Huan feared he might afterward grow suspicious; he went out and proclaimed that, empowered to command the provincial garrisons, the troops were to assemble east of the Fen for orders.

literal: He then raised the command banner at Yangqu Stream and set forth the organization.
idiomatic: At Yangqu Stream he raised his headquarters banner and organized his divisions.

literal: One came to the camp gate in submission wearing a red kerchief robe, calling himself the runner at Gengyang station, wishing to attend at left and right.
idiomatic: A man in a red kerchief and robe came to the gate, calling himself the Gengyang relay runner, and asked to serve at Gao Huan's side.

literal: Inquiring into him, he was known for strength and had often at Bingzhou market killed men in brawls; he was therefore appointed trusted attendant.
idiomatic: Inquiry showed he was famed for strength and had killed men in brawls at the Bingzhou market; Gao Huan made him a personal guard.

literal: The soldiers had long hated Zhao and delighted in Shenwu; hence none failed to come.
idiomatic: The troops had long hated Erzhu Zhao and welcomed Gao Huan, so all rallied to him.

literal: Before long, he again had Liu Gui ask Zhao, saying that Bing and Si had suffered frost and drought year after year, the surrendered households dug yellow rats to eat, all without grain color in their faces, merely fouling the realm's soil in vain — he asked that they be allowed to forage in Shandong and, once warm and fed, be settled and disposed of.
idiomatic: Before long Gao Huan sent Liu Gui to ask Zhao: Bing and Si had suffered frost and drought for years; surrendered households dug out yellow rats to eat, faces gaunt and wasted. Let them move east to forage in Shandong and settle once they are fed, he urged.

literal: Zhao followed this proposal.
idiomatic: Zhao agreed.

literal: His chief clerk Murong Shaozong remonstrated, saying: "It must not be done. Now the four quarters are in turmoil and men harbor divergent hopes; moreover High Duke Gao is heroic in strategy and holds great armies — this will not do.
idiomatic: His chief secretary Murong Shaozong warned, "You cannot do this. The realm is in turmoil and men turn their hopes elsewhere; Gao Huan is ambitious and now commands a great army—this cannot stand.

literal: " Zhao said: "We have sworn a solemn oath before the incense — what is there to worry about?
idiomatic: Zhao said, "We swore a blood oath at the incense altar—what is there to fear?"

literal: Shaozong said: "Even full brothers are thus hard to trust — how much less an oath before incense!
idiomatic: Shaozong replied, "Full brothers cannot trust each other—what use is a sworn oath?"

literal: At that time those at Zhao's side had already received Shenwu's gold; they therefore slandered Shaozong, saying he and Shenwu had old grudges; Zhao thereupon confined Shaozong and urged Shenwu to depart.
idiomatic: By then Zhao's attendants had taken Gao Huan's gold and accused Shaozong of an old feud with Gao Huan; Zhao imprisoned Shaozong and pressed Gao Huan to march.

literal: Shenwu then departed Jinyang through Fukou.
idiomatic: Gao Huan marched out of Jinyang through Fukou Pass.

literal: On the road he met the Northern Xiangchang Princess, wife of Erzhu Rong, coming from Luoyang with three hundred horses; he seized them all and exchanged for them.
idiomatic: On the road he met the Northern Xiangchang Princess, Erzhu Rong's widow, riding from Luoyang with three hundred horses—and seized every one.

literal: When Zhao heard, he released Shaozong and questioned him.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao heard, he released Shaozong and asked his meaning.

literal: Shaozong said: "It is still like something in the palm of the hand.
idiomatic: Shaozong said, "It is still something clasped in your palm.

literal: " Thereupon he himself pursued Shenwu.
idiomatic: He set out in pursuit himself.

literal: Reaching Xiangyuan, the Zhang River suddenly rose in flood and the bridge was destroyed.
idiomatic: At Xiangyuan the Zhang River had swollen and broken the bridge.

literal: Shenwu bowed across the water and said: "The reason I borrowed the princess's horses was for no other cause — only to guard against bandits in Shandong.
idiomatic: Gao Huan bowed from across the water and said, "I took the princess's horses only to provision against bandits in the east.

literal: Your Highness, having received the princess's words, came yourself in pursuit — if I cross the river now and die I will not refuse, but these troops will at once rebel.
idiomatic: You came because of her complaint—but if I ford the river now and die, I will not refuse; this army will rebel.

literal: " Zhao himself declared he had no such intent; thereupon he crossed lightly on horseback, sat with Shenwu under the tent, stated his apology, then handed over a knife and offered his neck, allowing Shenwu to behead him.
idiomatic: Zhao swore he meant no harm, rode across lightly, and sat with Gao Huan under the tent to apologize; he handed over a knife and offered his neck for Gao Huan to strike.

literal: Shenwu wept greatly and said: "Since the Heavenly Pillar passed away, on what does Heiliuhun anymore rely? I wish Your Lordship ten thousand years, that my strength may be employed.
idiomatic: Gao Huan wept and said, "Since the Heavenly Pillar died, Heiliuhun has no one else to serve. Live ten thousand years, my lord, that I may still put my strength at your use.

literal: Now others have built estrangement to this point — how can Your Lordship bear to speak thus again!
idiomatic: Others have driven this wedge between us—how can you speak so again!

literal: " Zhao threw the knife to the ground; they thereupon slaughtered a white horse and swore alliance, vowing brotherhood, and stayed the night drinking.
idiomatic: Zhao cast the knife aside; they sacrificed a white horse and swore brotherhood again, staying up drinking through the night.

literal: Jing concealed strong men intending to seize Zhao; Shenwu bit his arm to stop him, saying: "If we kill him now, his faction will surely flee and gather to reassemble.
idiomatic: Jing had hidden strong men ready to seize Zhao; Gao Huan bit his arm to stop him, saying, "Kill him now and his faction will scatter and regroup.

literal: The troops are hungry and the horses lean; we cannot sustain one another; if heroes rise up, the harm will be all the greater.
idiomatic: Our troops are hungry and our horses spent—we cannot afford a split. If some hero rises, the harm will be worse.

literal: Better for now to let him go.
idiomatic: Better to leave him be for now.

literal: Although Zhao is vigorous and swift, he is fierce, cunning, and without strategy — not worth contriving against.
idiomatic: Zhao is fierce but witless—not worth plotting against.

literal: " Next day Zhao returned to camp and again summoned Shenwu; Shenwu was about to mount his horse and go to him, but Sun Teng held his robe and stopped him.
idiomatic: Next day Zhao returned to camp and summoned Gao Huan again; Gao Huan was about to ride to him, but Sun Teng seized his robe and held him back.

literal: Zhao railed wantonly across the water and galloped back to Jinyang.
idiomatic: Zhao cursed him from across the river and galloped back to Jinyang.

literal: Zhao's trusted man Nianxian led the families of surrendered households in a separate encampment; Shenwu feigned friendship with him, observed the blade he wore at his belt, and took it to kill his followers; the followers all scattered.
idiomatic: Nianxian, a trusted man of Zhao's, camped apart with the families of surrendered households; Gao Huan feigned friendship, snatched the blade at his belt, and killed his escort—the rest scattered.

literal: Thereupon officers and troops were all pleased and doubly wished to attach themselves and follow.
idiomatic: The army rejoiced and rallied to him in greater numbers.

literal: Initially, inner-learning scholars under Wei Emperor Taiwu memorialized that Shangdang had the qi of a Son of Heaven, saying it was at Dawang Mountain in Huguan.
idiomatic: In Emperor Taiwu's day, court scholars reported that Shangdang bore the aura of an emperor—at Dawang Mountain in Huguan.

literal: Emperor Taiwu thereupon toured south to suppress and counter it, piled stones into three mounds, and cut down the northern Fenghuang Mountain to destroy its form.
idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu marched south to suppress it, piled stones into three cairns, and cut down Northern Fenghuang Mountain to break its form.

literal: Later those from Shangdang living at Jinyang were called Shangdang Ward; Shenwu actually dwelled there.
idiomatic: Later the Shangdang exiles at Jinyang lived in what was called Shangdang Ward—and Gao Huan had lived there.

literal: On this march he lodged at Dawang Mountain sixty days before advancing.
idiomatic: On this march he camped at Dawang Mountain for sixty days before advancing.

literal: About to exit Fukou, he doubly tightened discipline; not the slightest item was permitted to be plundered.
idiomatic: Before leaving Fukou he tightened discipline sharply—not the smallest thing might be taken.

literal: About to pass through wheat fields, Shenwu always walked leading his horse.
idiomatic: Passing wheat fields, he always led his horse on foot.

literal: Near and far hearing of it, all praised Commandant Gao for leading troops with stern order, and turned their hearts to him.
idiomatic: Near and far men praised Commandant Gao for his disciplined troops and gave him their hearts.

literal: He then advanced, encamped at Ye, and sought grain from Liu Dan, governor of Xiang Province; Dan did not supply it.
idiomatic: He marched on and encamped at Ye, but Liu Dan, governor of Xiang Province, refused him grain.

literal: There was rent rice at a military camp; Shenwu took it himself.
idiomatic: He took it himself from the military storehouses.

literal: In the second month of the first year of Putai of Wei, Shenwu's army halted at Xindu; Gao Gan and Feng Longzhi opened the gates to await him, and he thereupon seized Ji Province.
idiomatic: In the second month of Wei Putai 1 (531), Gao Huan halted at Xindu; Gao Gan and Feng Longzhi opened the gates, and he seized Ji Province.

literal: That month Erzhu Dulü deposed Yuan Ye and enthroned Emperor Jiemin, intending to restrain and attach Shenwu.
idiomatic: That month Erzhu Dulü deposed Yuan Ye and enthroned Emperor Jiemin, hoping to bind Gao Huan.

literal: In the third month he reported to Emperor Jiemin, enfeoffed Shenwu as Prince of Bohai, and summoned him to court audience.
idiomatic: In the third month he had Emperor Jiemin enfeoff Gao Huan as Prince of Bohai and summoned him to court.

literal: Shenwu declined.
idiomatic: Gao Huan declined.

literal: On the guisi day of the fourth month, he was further granted Eastern Route Grand Chief and First Chief of the Garrison Peoples.
idiomatic: On the guisi day of the fourth month he was further given Eastern Route Grand Chief and First Chief of the Garrison Peoples.

literal: Pang Cangying came fleeing from Taiyuan; Shenwu made him a clerk on the chief's staff, and soon after made him governor of An Province.
idiomatic: Pang Cangying fled from Taiyuan; Gao Huan made him a chief's clerk, then governor of An Province.

literal: Shenwu himself turned toward Shandong, nurtured soldiers and repaired armor, forbade pillaging, and the common people turned their hearts to him.
idiomatic: Turning east into Shandong, Gao Huan drilled troops and repaired armor, forbade pillaging, and won the people.

literal: He then forged a letter saying Erzhu Zhao would assign the Six Garrisons men to the Jie-Hu as retainers; the multitude all groaned with resentment.
idiomatic: He forged a letter claiming Erzhu Zhao would assign the Six Garrisons men to the Jie-Hu as retainers, and the army groaned with anger.

literal: He again forged an order from Bing Province, conscripting troops to campaign against the Buluoji.
idiomatic: He also forged a Bingzhou conscription order to fight the Buluoji.

literal: He mobilized ten thousand men and was about to send them off; Sun Teng and Jing asked that they be kept five days — twice thus.
idiomatic: He called up ten thousand men to send away; Sun Teng and Jing twice asked for a five-day delay.

literal: Shenwu personally escorted them to the suburbs, weeping as he clasped them in farewell; all wailed and lamented, the sound of crying shaking the earth.
idiomatic: Gao Huan escorted them to the suburbs himself, weeping as he took leave; the men wailed until the earth seemed to shake.

literal: Shenwu then explained to them: "I with you all lost our native places as sojourners; in duty we are one family — I did not expect those above would summon you thus.
idiomatic: Gao Huan told them, "We are all exiles from home, one family in name—I never thought they would summon you like this.

literal: Go straight west and you should die; fail the army deadline and again you should die; be assigned to the country's people and again you should die — what is to be done!
idiomatic: March west and you die; miss the deadline and you die; be handed to the Jie-Hu and you die—what can we do?

literal: " The multitude said: "Only rebellion remains!
idiomatic: The men cried, "We can only rebel!"

literal: " Shenwu said: "Rebellion is the urgent plan; we must choose one man as leader.
idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "Rebellion is the urgent move—but we must choose a leader.

literal: The multitude wished to uphold Shenwu.
idiomatic: They wanted Gao Huan.

literal: Shenwu said: "Your fellow-townsmen are hard to control — have you not seen Ge Rong?
idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "Your kind is hard to rule—have you forgotten Ge Rong?

literal: Though he had a million followers, without law and punishment he in the end perished to ash and extinction.
idiomatic: A million men, and without law he perished to nothing.

literal: Now taking me as leader, it must differ from before — you must not cheat the Han subjects, must not violate army commands; if life and death are entrusted to me then it can be done, otherwise it cannot be done, becoming the laughingstock of the realm.
idiomatic: Make me your leader and things will differ: no cheating Han subjects, no breaking army law. Give me your lives and I will lead you—or leave and be mocked by the realm.

literal: The multitude all prostrated their foreheads; life and death were as he commanded.
idiomatic: They bowed to the ground and pledged their lives to his command.

literal: Shenwu said, if there is no other way.
idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "If there is no other way."

literal: Next day he slaughtered an ox to feast the troops and explained the intent to campaign against the Erzhu.
idiomatic: Next day he slaughtered an ox to feast the troops and declared war on the Erzhu.

literal: Feng Longzhi came forward and said: "A moment once in a thousand years — all under heaven is greatly fortunate.
idiomatic: Feng Longzhi came forward and said, "A moment that comes once in a thousand years—all heaven is fortunate.

literal: " Shenwu said: "Punishing the rebels is great accord with righteousness;
idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "Punishing these rebels is righteousness itself;

literal: succoring the age is great enterprise.
idiomatic: saving the age is great endeavor.

literal: Though I am not martial, to follow with my death — how would I dare yield!
idiomatic: I am no warrior, but I will follow with my life—how could I refuse!"

literal: On the gengzi day of the sixth month he raised righteousness at Xindu, not yet openly turning against the Erzhu house.
idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the sixth month he raised the banner at Xindu, not yet openly breaking with the Erzhu.

literal: When Li Yuanzhong with Gao Gan pacified Yin Province and beheaded Erzhu Yusheng, coming to pay respects, Shenwu beat his breast and said: "Today rebellion is decided.
idiomatic: When Li Yuanzhong and Gao Gan took Yin Province and brought Erzhu Yusheng's head, Gao Huan struck his breast and said, "Today the break is made.

literal: " He thereupon made Yuanzhong governor of Yin Province.
idiomatic: He appointed Yuanzhong governor of Yin Province.

literal: At this time military might was already aroused; he thereupon submitted a memorial listing the Erzhu house's crimes.
idiomatic: His army's strength now shown, he submitted a memorial denouncing the Erzhu clan.

literal: Shilong and the others kept the memorial secret and did not transmit it.
idiomatic: Shilong and the rest suppressed the memorial and never forwarded it.

literal: In the eighth month Erzhu Zhao captured and overran Yin Province; Li Yuanzhong came fleeing to join him.
idiomatic: In the eighth month Erzhu Zhao took Yin Province and Li Yuanzhong fled to Gao Huan.

literal: Sun Teng held that with the court cut off and isolated, if they did not provisionally establish a Son of Heaven, then the multitude's expectations would have nothing to attach to.
idiomatic: Sun Teng argued that with the court cut off, only a provisional emperor could hold men's hopes.

literal: On the renyin day of the tenth month they upheld Prince Lang, son of Prince Zhangwu Rong and Bohai governor, as emperor, era name Zhongxing — this was the Deposed Emperor.
idiomatic: On the renyin day of the tenth month they enthroned Lang, son of Prince Zhangwu Rong and governor of Bohai, as emperor under the era Zhongxing—the later Deposed Emperor.

literal: At that time Dulü and Zhongyuan's armies halted at Yangping; Erzhu Zhao joined them.
idiomatic: Dulü and Zhongyuan halted at Yangping, and Erzhu Zhao joined them.

literal: Shenwu used Dou Tai's stratagem, set loose counter-intelligence; Dulü and Zhongyuan returned without battle.
idiomatic: Using Dou Tai's counsel, Gao Huan spread discord and Dulü and Zhongyuan withdrew without fighting.

literal: Shenwu thereupon defeated Zhao at Guang'a.
idiomatic: Gao Huan then defeated Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a.

literal: In the eleventh month he attacked Ye; Liu Dan, governor of Xiang Province, closed the city and held firm.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month he attacked Ye; Liu Dan, governor of Xiang Province, barred the gates and held firm.

literal: Shenwu raised earth mounds, dug tunnels, and in places erected great pillars; at one stroke he burned them, and the wall sank into the ground.
idiomatic: Gao Huan built earthworks and dug tunnels, propping them with great pillars that he burned at once—the walls collapsed into the earth.

literal: Ma Xiang was then magistrate of Tangyin; Shenwu called to him: "Prefect Ma!
idiomatic: Ma Xiang was magistrate of Tangyin; Gao Huan called out, "Prefect Ma!

literal: " Xiang, ashamed, fled.
idiomatic: Ashamed, Xiang fled.

literal: On the renwu day of the first month of the first year of Yongxi, he captured Ye city and held it.
idiomatic: On the renwu day of the first month of Yongxi 1 (532), he took Ye and held it.

literal: The Deposed Emperor advanced Shenwu to Grand Chancellor, Pillar-of-State Grand General, and Grand Preceptor.
idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor promoted Gao Huan to Grand Chancellor, Pillar-of-State Grand General, and Grand Preceptor.

literal: At this time righteousness was raised in Qing Province; Grand Commander Cui Lingzhen and Grand Commander Geng Xiang both sent envoys to submit and attach themselves.
idiomatic: At the same time Qing Province rose in rebellion; Grand Commanders Cui Lingzhen and Geng Xiang both sent envoys to submit.
